items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: the A&R man was Mitchell Ayres, I think, and Mitchell Ayres was there.

ctx.x: You mean the first recording with Cab?

Yeah, my first recording. That's where I made "Necessity", "The Hidy Ho Man", "That's Me"; "The Calloway Boogie" and I forgot what the other tune was, but we did four sides that day at the theatre there at 52nd Street and Broadway. We were recording at the theatre there, and the A&R man was Mitchell Ayres, I think, and Mitchell Ayres was there. That's when Cab made his speech, which I never forgot because I was very much impressed with it when he said, "Fellows, we're getting ready to go out on the road, and…
months. Don't get what you want; get what you need!" And I always remembered that speech, I never forgot it. That really stayed with me.
